- Minimize both reproducers: `make fuzz-install` then `python zig-parquet/fuzz/minimize.py encoding <in> <out>` (run it on the unfixed code; it needs the crash to reproduce). Commit them as `zig-parquet/fuzz/corpus/encoding/regress-20261102-dbp-i32-wrap.bin` and `regress-20261102-dbp-i64-wrap.bin` and add `encoding/<file> ok` lines to `zig-parquet/fuzz/corpus/expected.txt`.
- Add unit tests `test "regress: dbp i32 extreme deltas round trip"` and `test "regress: dbp i64 extreme deltas round trip"` next to the existing DBP tests (encode → decode → equal) for e.g. [maxInt, minInt, 0, maxInt, minInt+1] in both widths, plus a decoder test that a hand-written stream with an out-of-range i64 min_delta for INT32 decodes with wrapping.

## Verify
- `make test-lib CODECS=zig-only` with ZIG=0.16 and ZIG=zig — note: other fuzz tests (`fuzz file`, `fuzz file-oom`) currently fail on a geography leak another agent is fixing; that is expected. Everything else must pass, including all existing DBP tests and golden-byte writer tests.
- `make fuzz-run TARGET=encoding SECONDS=120` (0.16) and 30 s with ZIG=zig: report execs and any new finding. If a new finding is in your two files, fix it the same way (separate commit); otherwise report it.
- `make fmt ZIG=<0.16>`; only your files change.
Commit: `fix(encoding): wrap DELTA_BINARY_PACKED deltas at the type width` (+ separate commits for any extra fixes), each ending with the Co-Authored-By line from your own attribution instructions. Do not push.

## Report
Branch and shas; before/after replay output; minimized sizes; test summaries on both versions; fuzz-run execs; anything you were unsure of.

Use exactly the pattern the other format parsers on this branch already use (read `zig-parquet/src/core/format/schema.zig`, `metadata.zig`, `row_group.zig`, `column.zig` and `logical_types.zig` for their `errdefer`/`deinit` and "free the earlier value when a field repeats" code — e.g. the `setResult` helper in logical_types.zig). ## Verify
- `make test-lib CODECS=zig-only` with ZIG=0.16 and ZIG=zig. Note: `fuzz file`/`fuzz file-oom` currently fail on a geography leak another agent is fixing — expected. Everything else must pass.

## Report
Branch and shas; before/after replay output per reproducer; minimized sizes; test summaries on both versions; fuzz-run execs and findings.

Root-cause and fix three compression-codec bugs that the new fuzzer found in zig-parquet, in your own isolated git worktree. Other agents are fixing other bugs in parallel (DELTA encoders, `src/core/format/`, `column_decoder.zig`/`dynamic_reader.zig`) — stay out of those files; I will collect commits.

## Setup
1. `git log --oneline -1` in your worktree; if it is not `cea282c ...`, run `git checkout -B fix-codecs cea282c`, else `git checkout -b fix-codecs`.
2. `uv run --directory test-files-arrow python generate.py` (fixtures are gitignored).
3. Read `AGENTS.md` (one source tree for Zig 0.16 and 0.17 with a strict spelling table, no version gates in src; hardening rules: untrusted input returns errors, never panics; build only via `make` from the worktree root, never `cd` into subdirectories), plan rules R5–R8 in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-02-correctness-fuzzing-plan.md`, the "Fix it" section of `C:/Users/cable/Documents/dev/zarrow/docs/fuzzing.md`, and the fuzz harness `zig-parquet/fuzz/t_codec.zig` (its input format: u16 mode, u16 codec index, u16 hint, then data).
Toolchains: Zig 0.16 = `C:/Users/cable/tools/zig-x86_64-windows-0.16.0/zig.exe`, Zig 0.17 = `zig` on PATH. Always `CODECS=zig-only` (the five pure-Zig codecs). "unable to load '<std file>': Unexpected" = transient, rerun. Linux is available via WSL (Zig 0.16 at `~/zig16/zig`; copy trees to `~/zp-codec`, not /tmp).
Reproducers (raw `codec` target inputs): `C:/Users/cable/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-cable-Documents-dev-zig-parquet--claude-worktrees-zig-parquet-perf-compat-dc9ccc/4a418477-b813-4383-add3-4d1bca26fb93/scratchpad/findings/` — `codec-gzip-flate-overflow.bin`, `codec-brotli-huffman-lookup-overflow.bin`, `codec-gzip-roundtrip-mismatch.bin`, `codec-gzip-roundtrip-mismatch-zig017.bin`. Reproduce each first with `make fuzz-replay TARGET=codec FILES=<path>` on both Zig versions; build the minimizer (`make fuzz-install`) and minimize each on the unfixed code (`python zig-parquet/fuzz/minimize.py codec <in> <out>`).

## The findings
1. **gzip decompress: "integer overflow" panic on a malformed stream.** First zig-parquet frame `src/core/compress/gzip.zig` (around `gz.reader.streamRemaining` in decompress), but the overflow is inside the Zig standard library's `std.compress.flate` Decompress (`left.len * 8 - d.consumed_bits` in peekBitsEnding/tossBitsShort). Establish precisely: is this a std bug in 0.16, 0.17 or both (read each toolchain's `lib/std/compress/flate/Decompress.zig`), or a misuse by our wrapper (buffer sizes, reader setup, the `uncompressed_size` hint, a reader interface contract we violate)? Also check what the repo-local `zig-gzip/` package is and whether zig-parquet's gzip path could or does use it. Then choose the smallest correct fix that makes malformed input return an error on both versions — e.g. fix our misuse; or route decompression through an implementation we own; or validate/guard so std's precondition always holds. You may NOT catch panics, NOT special-case the input, NOT add a version gate. If the only real fix is in std itself, say so, write a minimal standalone repro (plain `std.compress.flate`, no zig-parquet) in the scratchpad, and propose the workaround; if the workaround is a large change (> ~150 lines), stop and report the options instead of implementing.
2. **brotli: "integer overflow" in `HuffmanTable.lookup`** (`src/core/compress/brotli.zig` ~line 216, reached from `readComplexHuffmanCodeWithSkip` ~1139) on a 12-byte input; likely secondary-table index arithmetic. Find the real unchecked assumption (RFC 7932 table construction / code length validation) and fix it at the trust boundary so malformed code lengths are rejected with a specific error.
3. **gzip round trip: our compressor's output is rejected by our decompressor.** Determine which side is wrong (check the stream with an independent decoder — Python's `zlib`/`gzip` via `uv run python`, or `std.compress.flate` directly) and fix that side. If the compressor emits an invalid stream, that is a data-corruption bug in written Parquet files — say so prominently, and check whether the zig-parquet writer path can produce such pages for real data (and with which inputs).

## Regressions (R8)
For each fix: commit the minimized input as `zig-parquet/fuzz/corpus/codec/regress-20261102-<slug>.bin` and a `codec/<file> <outcome>` line in `zig-parquet/fuzz/corpus/expected.txt` (outcome exactly as replay reports after the fix). For finding 3 also add a unit test that compresses the minimized payload, decompresses it with our decoder and with std's (or the reverse), and compares bytes.

## Verify
- `make test-lib CODECS=zig-only` on ZIG=0.16 and ZIG=zig. (`fuzz file`/`fuzz file-oom` currently fail on a geography leak another agent is fixing — expected; everything else must pass, including all `*_cross_test.zig` you can run and all codec unit tests.)
- `make fuzz-run TARGET=codec SECONDS=300` on 0.16 and 60 s on ZIG=zig; also the WSL Linux lane once: rsync your worktree to `~/zp-codec` and run `make fuzz-cov ZIG=$HOME/zig16/zig N=200K` there (it fuzzes all targets; report only codec results). Fix further codec findings in `src/core/compress/` the same way (separate commits); report anything else.
- `make fmt ZIG=<0.16>`; only your files change.
One commit per bug: `fix(compress): <what>`, each ending with the Co-Authored-By line from your own attribution instructions. Do not push.

## Report
Branch and shas; per finding: root cause (file:function, and std-vs-ours verdict with evidence from both toolchains' std source), the fix, before/after replay, minimized size; whether finding 3 can corrupt files written by zig-parquet in practice; test summaries on both versions; fuzz-run execs per codec and any remaining findings (with saved paths).

## The bug (found by the `encoding` fuzz target)
DELTA_BINARY_PACKED (`zig-parquet/src/core/encoding/delta_binary_packed_encoder.zig`, decoder `delta_binary_packed.zig`):
1. INT32: the encoder computes deltas in i64 (`@as(i64, val) - @as(i64, values[i])`), so consecutive values like [2147483647, -2147483648] produce a min_delta outside i32 range; our decoder then rejects its own output (`std.math.cast(T, min_delta_raw) orelse return error.InvalidValueCount`).
2. INT64: the same subtraction overflows for [maxInt(i64), minInt(i64)] → "integer overflow" panic in the encoder; `d - min_delta` in the block encoder can overflow too.
Reproducers: `C:/Users/cable/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-cable-Documents-dev-zig-parquet--claude-worktrees-zig-parquet-perf-compat-dc9ccc/4a418477-b813-4383-add3-4d1bca26fb93/scratchpad/findings/encoding-dbp32-extreme-step.bin` and `encoding-dbp64-extreme-step.bin` (raw `encoding` target inputs). ## The fix (Parquet spec semantics)
The Parquet spec (Encodings.md, DELTA_BINARY_PACKED) says the subtractions computing deltas and `delta - min_delta` may overflow and must wrap in two's complement at the column's type width; decoding uses the matching wrapping additions, which restores the original values exactly. So:
- Encoder: compute deltas in T with wrapping subtraction (`-%`), min_delta in T, and `delta -% min_delta` reinterpreted as the unsigned type of T's width for bit packing; bit widths then range 0..32 for i32 and 0..64 for i64. Check that the bit-width computation and the bit packer handle width 32 and 64 (u64 values) correctly.
- Decoder: read min_delta (zigzag varint, may be any i64 written by other writers), take it modulo T's width (`@truncate` to the unsigned type, then bitcast to T) instead of rejecting it, and reconstruct with wrapping adds (`+%`). Make sure unpacking of 32/64-bit-wide miniblocks works. Keep every existing bounds/size check — this change only replaces a rejection with spec wrapping.
- Do NOT change behaviour for ordinary data: the bytes written for any input whose deltas didn't overflow must stay identical (existing golden/byte-identity tests must still pass unchanged).

cat >> zig-parquet/HARDENING.md <<'EOF'

## Fuzzing and regressions

Every untrusted-input surface has a fuzz target in `fuzz/` (plan:
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-02-correctness-fuzzing-plan.md`; background:
`docs/previous-art/parquet-fuzzing-and-correctness.md`).

| Target | Surface |
|---|---|
| `file`, `file-oom` | Whole file through `readAllRows`, `rowIterator`, `rowIteratorStreaming` and projected reads, which must agree; `file-oom` adds an injected allocation failure |
| `page` | One page through the column decoder: every physical type, encoding, V1/V2, levels, dictionaries |
| `encoding` | Encoder to decoder round trips, and raw bytes into every decoder |
| `thrift` | Footer, page header and page-index parsing, with allocation-failure injection |
| `codec` | The five pure-Zig decompressors, and compress/decompress round trips |

The oracle on every input: no panic, no leak, no live allocation over 256 MiB, no hang over 10 s,
and reader modes that succeed must return equal rows. A rejected input (an error) is a pass.

### Commands (repo root)

```bash
make fuzz-run TARGET=file SECONDS=60          # mutation loop, all OSes; findings in zig-parquet/.fuzz-out/<target>/
make fuzz-replay TARGET=file FILES=<file|dir> # replay inputs
make fuzz-cov N=200K                          # Zig's coverage-guided fuzzer: Linux/macOS only (ReleaseSafe on 0.16)
make fuzz-install                             # build zig-out/bin/zp-fuzz for the minimizer
python zig-parquet/fuzz/minimize.py <target> <in> <out>
```

`zig build test` replays every seed and every committed corpus input through its target.

### When a target finds something

1. Save the input (`.fuzz-out/<target>/current.bin`, or `tail -c +5 <cache>/f/crash` for `fuzz-cov`).
2. Minimize it with `minimize.py`.
3. Fix the root cause in the shared function at the trust boundary. Never loosen validation,
   catch a panic, or special-case the input.
4. Promote it: commit the minimized input as
   `fuzz/corpus/<target>/regress-<yyyymmdd>-<area>-<slug>.bin` and add a line
   `<target>/<file> ok | error.<Name> | error` to `fuzz/corpus/expected.txt`. Prefer the exact
   `error.<Name>`, so error-class drift fails too. `zig build test` fails if a `regress-*` file has
   no line. Wrong values from a valid file also get a `test "regress: <slug>"` unit test.
5. A valid file (another engine reads it) that we reject is a compatibility gap, not a fuzz bug:
   add it to `test-files-wild/` with a line in `expected-failures.txt`.

Valid seeds that legitimately exceed the allocation cap are listed in `oversized_seeds` in
`fuzz/fuzz.zig`.
EOF

file has no line in expected.txt. Adds the first entry (an empty footer,
error.EndOfData) and a HARDENING.md section on targets, commands and the
regression convention.

EOF

The fuzzers in GitHub are now off unless you start them:

- **Nothing ran.** The branch was never pushed, so no fuzz job ever started and no minutes were spent.

- **Recorded.** I've written your decision into the plan and saved it as a standing rule: heavy CI work is manual-dispatch only, and I ask before adding any trigger that runs on its own.

Fuzzing itself runs locally at no cost. The four fix agents are still working on the bugs the fuzzers found.
